findings.reason: §6 is marked done on a measure that its own artifact fails, so the plan reports a landed section whose stated success condition is unmeetable until §9 lands, and the reader who trusts the tick treats the last clause of §6 as satisfied.
findings.text: §6 is declared done (plan-section-declarations s6=done) on the done-when "every command and row word it names exists on reckon's main", and the row word it names is "A reckon monitor row reading `usage limit reset`"; §9:145 records that the only such row this line has ever drawn read `14:32:38  limit  claude-sub  new → working  –` — "a state transition and no words" — and confirms in source that no pane can print that phrase, because `reckon/crew/ticker.py` contains zero occurrences of `detail` and therefore drops the clause carrying it, so the clause exists only in the producer's stream row (`~/.config/reckon/crew/watch/reckon-18dc8a86709b.events`, field `detail`)

findings.reason: the section body is the text a later node copies, so it hands the next announcer the exact group the plan's own §9 and the live incident record as the defect.
findings.text: §6 quotes the paragraph it landed, and that quoted text announces with `reckon crew budget --reset --group claude-sub --used --reason "<what the lead said>"`, but the commit §6 names as its landing (dotfiles `fabae49`, "docs(agents): announce a usage-limit reset once, for orchestrators only") records the paragraph as `--reset --used --group claude-orchestrators --clock five_hour --reason "<the lead's words>"`, and the plan's own §6 outcome comment (line 252) says the paragraph was "revised by the lead's ruling: announce under claude-orchestrators" — the plan's body text was never updated to the revised artifact, and it is the pre-ruling text §9 (line 145) exists to correct, since §6's version tells a session to announce under the worker lane's group

findings.reason: the declared graph is what a dispatcher reads to decide a section is ready, and without the edge §8 reads as dispatchable independently of the investigation whose findings define its write paths.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` carries entries for s2, s3, s4, s5, s6 and s9 only, so §8 declares no dependency on §7, although §8's Why line reads "§7 found why the `claude` account's windows have read `unknown` ... Its report is in the landing record under §7" and §8's three deliverables repair exactly the three causes §7 returned

findings.reason: the abbreviation does not move §9's mechanism or remedy, whose premise (a row drawn with the clause dropped at render) I confirmed directly in the stream and in `ticker.py`.
findings.text: §9 cites the 12:32 UTC announcement as `reckon crew budget --reset --used --group claude-sub --clock five_hour` with no `--reason`, but §1:58 landed `--reason` as required for `--reset --used` (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2861`, `raise click.UsageError` — `"--reason is required with --reset --used"`) and the store record for that event (`<crew-home>/budget-resets.json`, id `reset-claude-sub-20261022T123236Z`) carries `"reason": "the lead reports the usage limits have reset; every session continues its work"`, so the quoted command is not the one that produced the row §9 reasons from

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited module, symbol, test file, evidence anchor (#s1, #s2, #s5, #s6, #s7), the cross-plan section the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches#s83 and dotfiles commit fabae49 resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6 is declared done on a done-when whose row-word clause its own landed artifact does not satisfy.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gates write under the run directory, §7's report under the crew reports directory, §4/§6 into the landing record; no evidence home is a session scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the names the plan introduces (_reset_detail, sweep_resets, limit-reset, the stage word limit, the new test filenames) are mechanism names; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag is carried into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §6's quoted paragraph names the worker lane's budget group, which its own landed commit records as replaced; the other three checks hold, and §9's root cause is confirmed against the live stream.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one deliverable (the producer sweep and the pane row in §2 are one outcome, a reset reaching every pane once).
